H1.note: the APOE claim is on the e4 allele, where the causal chain starts (H1.3); H1.1 (APOE binds TREM2) is a rel and isoform-neutral. TREM2's sign is the mechanism's: TREM2 supports productive Abeta clearance, whose loss raises risk.

H2.note: signs from the title ('protective TREM2–DAP12 signaling') and mechanism ('insufficient PLCG2 output or excessive INPP5D braking reduces ... chemotaxis, endocytosis').

H3.note: the chain ends at 'Alzheimer's disease pathology', read as severity; the hypothesis makes no risk claim. TREM2's sign from the title ('protective TREM2 microglial state').

H4.note: the chain starts at TREM2–PLCG2 signaling, so the claim is ABI3's (the hypothesis's own gene). ABI3 appears only as a qualifier ('ABI3-dependent cytoskeletal remodeling'), so no statement starts at ABI3. Ends at 'Alzheimer's disease pathology', read as severity.

H5.note: no disease claim: the title calls LPIN2 a 'non-genetic modifier of microglial TREM2–PLCG2 responses' and neither title nor mechanism gives a direction on AD. The chain ends at Abeta clearance; the sign is the mechanism's ('reduced LPIN2 ... impairing sustained Abeta phagocytosis').

findings.detail: H1.2 ends at Abeta uptake and degradation; H1.3 starts at APOE4, so the APOE4 arm never passes through TREM2 binding (H1.1), the hypothesis's actual mechanism.
'microglial Abeta42 uptake and degradation', 'productive TREM2-dependent amyloid clearance' and 'reduced productive amyloid clearance' are one node (GO:0150094) under three labels; merged.
Neither H1.3 citation mentions clearance: rs429358 is an age-of-onset row with allele '?', PMID:8346443 is e4 dose versus AD risk; both support APOE4 -> AD, which is no step of the chain.

PMID:27025652 says APOE4 'has been found to impair Abeta clearance from the brain', nearest to H1.3, but the run cited it at H1.4; and it is general clearance, not the TREM2-dependent uptake the run's own H1.3 note calls unproven.
Confidence 'high', yet the run's own note says H1.3 is the unproven step, and no cited text states H1.3 or H1.4.
The TREM2 UniProt text lists APOE2, APOE3 and APOE4 as ligands alike; the binding step is isoform-neutral and cannot carry the APOE4-specific claim.
Almost every node has an empty CURIE, and the disease is written 'EFO:MONDO_0004975', a malformed CURIE for MONDO:0004975.
DAG and IP3 are typed 'process' (they are chemicals), and 'APOE-containing lipoproteins' is typed 'protein' (a particle).
TREM2 activates PLCG2 rests on a STRING edge with no experimental channel and two Reactome enrichment rows; nothing states activation.
H2.2 ends at DAG and IP3; H2.3 starts at INPP5D.
H2.3 ends at PI3K signaling; H2.4 starts at 'balanced PLCG2 activation and INPP5D inhibition', so PI3K signaling leads nowhere.
'balanced PLCG2 activation and INPP5D inhibition' can mean inhibition of INPP5D or by INPP5D, and 'balanced' implies a set point; the INPP5D sign was taken from the mechanism and falsification test.
The three MGI annotations are undirected 'abnormal' phenotypes, one in dendritic cells and one for Trem2 rather than PLCG2 or INPP5D.
GWAS rows (rs72824905, rs10933431, rs75932628, rs1582763, rs616338) are cited for process-to-disease steps; they state gene-level variant associations, which support no step of any chain.
Confidence 'high', but only the dead-end steps H2.2 and H2.3 have a citation that states them; H2.1, H2.4 and H2.5 have none.

PMID:41435829 (knockout, overexpression, antibodies, NHP and mouse) finds MS4A4A negatively regulates TREM2; the only support is a title-only conference abstract (PMC12738020). The run did flag it as contradicting.

PMC12738020 is cited at H3.3, but its title states the hypothesis's overall claim (MS4A4A 'reduces amyloid pathology'), not that the microglial response lowers pathology; no step runs from MS4A4A to pathology, so it supports only H3.1.
'protective microglial plaque response' is vague; grounded as microglial cell activation (GO:0001774), with 'protective' being the claim H3.3 makes.

H3 is falsified 'if deletion consistently increases functional surface TREM2 and plaque compaction'; the run's own contradicting citation PMID:41435829 already reports that MS4A4A knockout and degrading antibodies raise TREM2, and that MS4A4A 'limits microglia viability, phagocytosis, and lysosomal function', against the mechanism's 'protective phagocytic state'. The run keeps confidence 'medium' and support 'grounded'.

The run cites 'PMID:PMC12738020', a PMC id under a PMID prefix; the record is a conference abstract (pubType 'Abstract', journal supplement) with only a title, which the mechanism calls 'one disease-model report'.
ABI3 appears only as a qualifier ('ABI3-dependent cytoskeletal remodeling'), never as a step's subject, so the hypothesis's own gene has no route to the disease.
H4.1 cites only text-mined STRING edges and the ABI3 UniProt entry; the run's own note admits no direct step was shown.
The cited ABI3 UniProt text says ABI3 'in vitro, reduces cell motility', against the mechanism's claim that ABI3 organises remodeling needed for microglial migration (no step carries migration).

PMID:42092345 shows Abi3 S212F reduces dense-core compaction while lowering dense-core burden and leaving total Abeta unchanged; it supports neither remodeling -> compaction nor loss of compaction -> more pathology.
The contradicting AGR record (no Abi3 phenotype) is absence of annotation, not a null result, and the run's own chain citation PMID:42092345 reports an Abi3 mouse with phenotypes.

PMID:42092345, cited at H4.2 and H4.3, states the one link with a direction that involves ABI3 ('Abi3S212F produced a dysfunctional microglial state that reduced dense-core plaque compaction'), the mechanism's 'risk alleles weaken this response, producing less compact plaques'; no step carries ABI3 or its risk allele, so it supports nothing.
Confidence 'medium' and support 'grounded', yet no cited text states any of H4.1, H4.2 or H4.3, and the hypothesis's own gene appears only as a qualifier.
The falsification describes introducing the ABI3 risk allele 'despite matched ABI3 expression', but labels the perturbation action 'knockout'.
H5.1 ends at DAG; H5.2 starts at 'LPIN2-dependent phospholipid remodeling', so the run's own steps give LPIN2 no route past DAG (bridge B1 supplies one).
H5.2 ends at the TREM2–PLCG2 response; H5.3 starts again from lipid remodeling (H5.2's subject), skipping the response.

Bridge B1 (LPIN2 -> phospholipid metabolism) comes from the run's own LPIN2 UniProt citation (PC and PE biosynthesis); it makes explicit the 'LPIN2-dependent' qualifier the chain never states as a step, and treats biosynthesis as part of the run's 'remodeling'.
The chain ends at Abeta clearance and never reaches Alzheimer's disease; the hypothesis gives no disease direction.
No citation for H5.2 or H5.3 mentions lipid remodeling acting on TREM2, PLCG2 or clearance; the run's own note calls H5.2 speculative, yet the hypothesis is labelled 'grounded'.
Supporting citation R-HSA-9029569 (NR1H3/NR1H2 cholesterol efflux pathway enrichment) is cited at no step and states none.
Supporting citation AGR:MGI:3643932:MP:0002451 (Ms4a4a knockout, 'abnormal macrophage physiology') is cited at no step and states none.
RNPS1 is listed as unexplained; no hypothesis places it.
BLN:APOE-e4: no PR term for the APOE4 isoform and no allele term for APOE e4, which has no single dbSNP id.
BLN:MicroglialPlaqueEncasement and BLN:AmyloidPlaqueCompaction: no GO, HP or MP term for microglia wrapping plaques or for plaque compaction.

A gene-dependent process ('ABI3-dependent cytoskeletal remodeling', 'LPIN2-dependent phospholipid remodeling', 'TREM2-dependent clearance') has no node or ctx form; dropping the gene removes ABI3 from H4 entirely.
A protein complex ('TREM2–DAP12 receptor complex') has no entity form; grounded as TREM2.
A set point ('balanced' activation and inhibition, too much or too little both harmful) has no form; split into monotone effects.
'sustained' (a response that lasts under chronic stimulation) cannot be held; dropped.

Metabolite pools ('biosynthetic DAG' versus signalling DAG, which the run itself says differ) have no direct form: a pool is defined by its pathway, but ctx has no slot for a chemical's pathway (stage is happens_during, for processes). Biosynthetic DAG is held as DAG refined to the ER membrane, the place the cited LPIN2 text gives, standing in for the pathway.

No rule for a citation that states the step for a parent process or cell class (Abeta clearance in general versus by uptake and degradation; myeloid versus microglial chemotaxis); parent_disease covers diseases only.
PMC12738020 is a conference abstract with only a title; its design is unknown, so 'inVitro' is a placeholder.
Taxon has no non-human primate; PMID:41435829 spans macrophages, microglia, NHPs and a mouse model, recorded as mouse.

The LPIN2 UniProt function text carries no 'By similarity' marker, but its evidence code (ECO:0000250 from Q99PI5) shows it is inferred from another species; recorded as crossSpecies only by reading the metadata.
The PLCG2 UniProt quote names the enzyme class ('phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C enzymes'), not PLCG2 itself; kept as the entry's own function text.

audit.item: findings H3 (PMID:41435829 vs the H3 falsification)
audit.reason: H3 is falsified if deleting MS4A4A raises functional TREM2 and plaque compaction. The run's own contradicting citation PMID:41435829 already reports the TREM2 half (knockout and degrading antibodies raise TREM2) and says MS4A4A limits microglial phagocytosis and lysosomal function, against the 'protective phagocytic state'. Confidence stays 'medium', support 'grounded'.

The run cites a PMC id under a PMID prefix, and treats a title-only conference abstract (pubType 'Abstract', journal supplement) as 'one disease-model report'. The curator flagged the malformed disease CURIE but not this.

The paper states the ABI3-variant-to-compaction link the mechanism relies on, with a direction ('risk alleles ... producing less compact plaques'). No step carries ABI3 or its allele, so it supports nothing. The curator's findings record only what the paper does not show.

H4 is rated 'medium' and 'grounded', yet no cited text states H4.1, H4.2 or H4.3, and the hypothesis's own gene (ABI3) appears only as a qualifier. H1 and H2 got this finding; H4 is as bad and lacked one.

The falsification introduces the ABI3 risk allele 'despite matched ABI3 expression' but labels the perturbation action 'knockout'. A sibling AD curation flagged the same kind of action/description mismatch.
